original_card.question: Can a new local cost interface change the deficit-to-recursive-cost ratio beyond current packing?
methods: Propose a changed helper inventory and derive an optimistic exact moment.
Design a small completed instance and independently verify its endpoint and rank bill.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A new physically realizable contract, not another mixture already covered by the frozen catalogue.

first_step.inspect: Read the frozen catalogue bound exclusions and select one genuinely different helper endpoint inventory.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write the complete optimistic child histogram and reject it immediately if even the relaxation has insufficient headroom.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Helper inventory changes can improve the moment; repacking a covered cost interface cannot evade its scoped bound.
allowed_variations: Narrow to one changed boundary or helper type with explicit counts.
scope_change_triggers: Mixing only providers already inside the pinned catalogue.

actual_scope: On the pinned PR1094 gauge44 histogram, certify the pure-deletion threshold of rank mass 1 versus 2 and the eight-for-one rank-8 coalescence threshold 42 versus 43, uniformly across all 144 calls, at the selected bit endpoint.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a new realizable helper contract. This package keeps the pinned width multiset, call count, idle remainder, and observed mass identity, and prices two explicit endpoint edits. It does not mix frozen-catalogue providers and does not claim a scalar word. The refinement decides whether those edits have moment headroom before a circuit search.
bottleneck_link: The complex primitive binds. These are the smallest edits in the two stated families that push the selected complex moment strictly below one at the bit endpoint. A later contract with the same child delta must clear these counts; the screen itself does not change kappa.
stop_rule: Stop once the exact signs for mass 1, both mass-2 deletions, and coalescence counts 42 and 43 are certified, with the per-mass order and published endpoint controls. Do not search the canonical word or rerun the selected cold replay in this session.
evidence: verify.py prints PASS_GAUGE44_HELPER_ENDPOINT_SCREEN. Chooser seed ef87d06bc5be1f65ff317cc1c45c907b. Overlap search at 2026-11-06T12:17:07Z, complete open-PR and discussion pagination, did not find this threshold. Selected kappa is unchanged.

open_questions.question: Does the pinned gauge44 word contain a pure deletion of two rank units in every call, or 43 disjoint eight-for-one rank-8 replacements, with an empty restoration and frame bill?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Either edit is the first histogram in this screen that meets the bit endpoint, and every smaller copy of the same edit is excluded.
open_questions.first_step: Count disjoint rank-1 and rank-8 frame events in the canonical local word and reject any candidate that adds a child or a restoration.
open_questions.blocked_by: The paid histogram does not identify movable children. Extraction, routing, and dirty restoration are not priced here.

open_questions.question: If a helper width outside {4,5,7,8,9} is added, does paid mass remain M+1856, or does the new helper add a child that consumes the two-unit surplus?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The mass-2 deletion meets the bit endpoint only when those two units are not replaced by a new positive-rank child.
open_questions.first_step: Write one width-6 endpoint law and its exact child delta, then rerun this screen on that delta.
open_questions.blocked_by: No width-6 endpoint law is proved in this package.
